Thanks Aisha — that recap looks accurate. A few clarifications from Acme Health (legal + security sign-off needed):

- Confirmed: Acme Health requires a full opt-out from any model training/improvement that uses customer-provided content or derived logs. The opt-out must be account-scoped and documented in the DPA.
- Data residency: all user content and identifiable logs must be stored and processed in the EU (we prefer Frankfurt region).
- Retention: audit logs and metadata may be retained for up to 90 days; debug-level payloads should be pseudonymized and kept no longer than 30 days unless retained for an active incident investigation (with notification).
- PII: we are preparing a short list of fields that must be redacted/pseudonymized prior to any long-term storage.

I attached our initial DPA redlines for your legal team to review: Acme_DPA_Redlines_20280718.pdf

Please loop in Security/Legal and confirm whether Redwood can: 1) support an account-level training opt-out; 2) guarantee EU-only processing for the account; and 3) provide an exportable audit log that we can pull on-demand.

Best,
Elena Morales

Elena — thanks for the detail and for sending the redlines. Looping in Rishi from Security/Privacy to confirm technical and contractual scope.

High-level feasibility and proposed implementation plan from our side:
- Training opt-out: supported. We can set an account-level flag that prevents your tenant traffic and logs from being included in any model training or evaluation corpora. This is logged and auditable.
- EU-only processing: we can route and process the account exclusively in the eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) region and restrict cross-region backups. We’ll surface the region SLA and data flow diagram to your team.
- Retention & logs: default audit logs available for 90 days; we can configure a separate debug log stream (pseudonymized) with 30-day retention. All logs are encrypt-at-rest and in transit.

Attachments: Opt-out-confirmation-template.txt (short written confirmation we usually add to the DPA)

Rishi — can you confirm the above and provide a short checklist for the DPA and technical controls (exportable audit logs, KM integration, and region pinning)? We’ll draft the contract language and share it with Acme legal.

Hi Elena / Tom — Rishi from Security/Privacy here. Confirming Redwood’s options and next steps so Acme legal/security can proceed: 

1) Training opt-out (supported):
- We will mark Acme Health’s tenant with an explicit \"training_on_customer_data=false\" flag at the account level. Any data (user messages, uploads, derived embeddings, debug payloads) will be excluded from our model training pipelines and from datasets used for research/evals.
- This exclusion is enforced at the ingestion layer and audited; we can provide an attestation for the DPA.

2) Data residency (supported):
- Account pinning to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) for storage and inference. No cross-region replication for primary data; backups can be configured per contract.

3) Logging & retention:
- Audit logs (who/what/when) available and exportable; default retention = 90 days.
- Debug payloads: pseudonymization available; default retention = 30 days unless retained for a documented incident (with customer approval).

4) Key management & encryption:
- We support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM integrations for enterprise plans.

Next steps / deliverables from Redwood:
- Draft DPA amendment including the training opt-out clause and region pinning language (we’ll return with suggested contract text by EOD 2028-07-20).
- Provide a technical checklist link and a short attestation PDF that you can attach to the DPA.

Attachments: Redwood_Training_OptOut_Process.pdf
